subject: Deal velocity containment and rollback matrix
content:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Zhang <michael.zhang@globex.com>, Globex Procurement <procurement@globex.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Hi Dylan,

Quick update from our side — internal evaluation of the security controls + an extra legal review pushed our internal sign-off timeline out by two weeks. We were tracking to 11/12 as the close date, but procurement just informed me they now need until 11/26 to complete final counter-signature.

That said, we want to avoid a hard stop on production planning. Can you share a short containment plan that lets us:
- freeze the current deployment config so our engineering teams can continue staging work;
- preserve pricing on the table for 30 days; and
- identify a technical fallback if the number of concurrent seats requested exceeds initially provisioned capacity at go-live?

Appreciate a concise plan we can attach to our internal change request.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Sr. Director, Product Operations
Globex Corporation

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads-up and totally understand. High level response below; attaching a one-page containment snapshot and a technical rollback matrix (cc'd team).

Quick containment options we can enact immediately:
1) Pricing hold: we will lock the current quoted price for 30 days from 10/28 (will reflect in a revised quote PDF).
2) Deployment freeze: we can pin the staging environment to the currently provisioned Dedicated pool (no changes to runtime) so your engineers can finish integration without provisioning drift.
3) Capacity fallback: implement a two-tier canary — a short burst window (72 hours) that auto-scales to a compatible quantized model variant and an emergency throttling policy that preserves latency SLO for top-priority routes.

Next steps I propose:
- Today: Redwood provides updated MAP v3 (attached) and a short Canary_Fallback_Plan.
- By 11/04: joint sign-off on the revised MAP; procurement uses snapshot for change request.
- By 11/20: final validation run (non-prod) with canary enabled.

Marissa, can you confirm commercial language and whether we can offer bridge credits if the close slips beyond 30 days? Karthik — see note below for technical specifics.

Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: GLOBEX_MAP_v3.xlsx, Canary_Fallback_Plan.pdf

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Samantha — appreciate the heads up. From a commercial perspective:
- We can honor the quoted list price for 30 days starting 10/28. If the close extends between 31–60 days, we can provide a one-time bridge credit equal to 10% of first-month committed spend to mitigate procurement timing issues.
- Any extension beyond 60 days will be re-priced to current list rates; we'll document this in the revised MAP.

I will add these terms to clause 3.1 in the MAP and circulate a redline to procurement. Dylan — please confirm if that sits OK for legal.

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Hi all — adding the technical containment matrix. Key points: 
- Canary plan: we recommend a two-stage canary (10% of traffic -> 50% -> full) but for an abbreviated window tied to the tentative go-live, we can use a 10% warm-up + 40% burst model that relies on our quantized variant (6-bit) to keep latency within 1.2x baseline.
- KV cache warmup: preserve last-successful cache snapshot from staging to reduce cold-start token costs; KMS keys remain unchanged so there is no re-encryption needed on final cutover.
- Emergency throttling: route-based throttles for non-critical endpoints (analytics, background embeddings) to preserve core conversational flows.

I'll attach a short tech note and the rollback matrix. If procurement needs a short explanatory appendix about the quantized variant, I can draft it.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment referenced: Canary_Fallback_Plan.pdf

---

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Zhang <michael.zhang@globex.com>, procurement@globex.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Thanks all — that helps a lot. Two quick asks from procurement and engineering:
- Procurement: can you provide the MAP v3 redline and the 30/60-day clause text as a single PDF we can attach to the internal change request (procurement@globex.com)?
- Engineering: Michael requests a one-hour tech walkthrough on 11/05 to validate the canary behavior and KV warmup process.

If we can get both items by COB 11/03, procurement will accept the 11/26 target for signature and proceed with internal approvals.

Samantha

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@globex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & close cadence - possible delay

Thanks — quick status and agreed actions (finalizing for procurement package):

Agreed re-baseline:
- New target signature date: 2026-11-26 (procurement snapshot attached).
- Price hold: 30 days starting 2026-10-28; 31–60 day bridge credit = 10% of month-one committed spend.
- Escalation: if signature slips >60 days, Marissa will notify executive sponsor and we will reconvene a pricing review.

Immediate deliverables (owner / due):
- GLOBEX_MAP_v3 redline PDF (Marissa) / due 2026-11-03 COB -> marissa.cole@redwood.com
- Canary technical appendix + rollback matrix (Karthik) / due 2026-11-03 COB -> karthik_iyer@redwood.com
- One-hour walkthrough scheduled with Michael Zhang and engineering (Dylan to set invite) / target 2026-11-05 10:00-11:00 PT

Fallback commitments:
- If production demand spikes beyond provisioned capacity at go-live, Redwood will:
  * initiate emergency throttling for non-critical routes;
  * open a temporary burst to quantized model variant for 72 hours;
  * provide a post-mortem and cost reconciliation within 10 business days.

I'll prepare the procurement packet (single PDF) after I receive Marissa's redline and Karthik's appendix; aiming to deliver before the 11/03 COB deadline.

Thanks everyone — will send the calendar invite in the next 30 minutes.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced in-thread: GLOBEX_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet: MAP milestones & terms), Canary_Fallback_Plan.pdf (technical appendix, rollback matrix).
